newsitem.title: USA: FoxMeyer Drug seeks conversion to Chapter 7.
newsitem.headline: FoxMeyer Drug seeks conversion to Chapter 7.

text.p: Avatex Corp affiliate FoxMeyer Drug Co and five units have asked the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware for approval to convert from Chapter 11 reorganization status to Chapter 7 liquidation.

In court papers filed Tuesday, they said the purpose of the conversion is to "obtain a consensual plan of liquidation pursuant to which their assets...could be fairly distributed among their remaining liabilities."

FoxMeyer said monthly administration costs as high as $2 million and a pending lawsuit were among the factors for converting to Chapter 7 because a liquidation trustee would be "a central source of control" for reducing costs and managing litigation.
"The debtors believe that a conversion will serve the best interests of their estates, creditors and stockholders and will not prejudice the rights of any party in these cases," court papers say.

In their motion for conversion, the FoxMeyer entities have asked that it be made effective Tuesday at 1700 EST/2200 GMT and that the creditors meet promptly to choose a liquidation trustee. The motion is expected to be presented at a hearing already scheduled before bankruptcy Judge Helen Balick Tuesday at 1500 EST/2000 GMT.
FoxMeyer was one of the largest wholesale drug distribution companies in the U.S. before its bankruptcy filing on August 27, 1996.
